Lisa, if you visit a point 3 times, you must pool the data for the 3=20
visits, and record the effort as 3. So you'll have just one row for=20
that point. You won't get good estimates by point, and nor will they be =

independent, which invalidates the regression you plan to do. It is=20
better to model the counts by point, using a glm with a log link, and an =

offset to take account of detectability. The following paper outlines=20
how this can be done, but Distance isn't set up to allow you to do this=20
I'm afraid.

Steve Buckland

Buckland, S.T., Russell, R.E., Dickson, B.G., Saab, V.A., Gorman, D.N. an=
d Block, W.M. 2009. =20
Analysing designed experiments in distance sampling. /Journal of Agricu=
ltural, Biological and Environmental Statistics/ *14*, 432-442.



On 12/09/2010 18:06, Lisa Baril wrote:
> > Hello
> >
> > I am a new to distance sampling and have a few questions regarding its =
use even after having read Intro to Distance Sampling and the user manual=
as well as browsing the forum. I have bird point transect data collected=
over 3 years with 2 to 3 visits each year for each of 67 points (althoug=
h some points were not surveyed at all during the first year) stratified =
over 3 habitat types. Observations were recorded as being in one of 4, 1=
0 m wide distance intervals. My goal is to obtain point-level density est=
imates for each of several bird species so that I can calculate density w=
ithin each habitat type. I need point level density estimates as these d=
ata will be used in regression analyses. To make things as simple as pos=
sible I have created text files for each species in each habitat type and=
will use year as a covariate. Below is an example subset for one species=
for one habitat type. The stratum layer is represtented by year, the s=
ample layer contains point count labels and survey effort, and observatio=
n is the radial distance at the midpoint of the distance interval they we=
re recorded. My questions are:1) Is this the correct way to set up the d=
ata?; 2) How do I account for variation in survey effort when building mo=
dels - do I obtain density estimates per point and then divide them mysel=
f by 2 or 3 or does distance do this for you? I really appreciate anyone=
's advice on this.
